# PROCESS — cand_0003 (iteration 3/3)

Parent champion: cand_0002 (val 0.533). I KEEP every cand_0002 lever verbatim (they
broke nothing and fixed 22/25) and ADD new, zero-/low-regression fixes for the clusters
cand_0002 left unresolved (12, 17, 23, 37, 40 + flaky 8, 11). Diagnosed THIS iteration's
`./trajectories/` directly (30 trials). No subagents — single-pass diagnosis was enough.

## Ranked clusters (leverage = failing tasks × trials × recoverable score)

| rank | cluster | tasks | type | lever |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | STALL: described-but-never-executed write (agent asks "reply yes", user says "yes###STOP###", episode ends before the write) | 40 (3/3), contributes 12, 37-t0 | BEHAVIORAL/DECISION | prompt R7 + base-confirm reconcile |
| 2 | Partial-transfer: bundles feasible+infeasible requests, transfers wholesale, skips the writes it COULD do | 37-t0 (1/3) | DECISION | prompt R8 |
| 3 | Cabin change done as cancel+NEW booking instead of in-place update; "basic economy flights can't be modified" over-applied to cabin | 11-t2 (1/3) | KNOWLEDGE/DECISION | prompt R4 strengthen |
| 4 | Wrong dob when the passenger becomes a DIFFERENT person (account holder): reused the replaced passenger's dob | 17 (2/3) | KNOWLEDGE + CODE | tools guard + prompt R2 split (a)/(b) |
| 5 | Conditional fallback fired on the wrong trigger (dropped 2nd passenger on no-seats, though fallback was gated on price>$500) | 8-t0 (1/3) | DECISION | prompt R9 |
| 6 | Replace-with-new-bookings but original NOT cancelled (both old + new left in DB) | 23 (3/3, complex) | BEHAVIORAL | prompt R10 |

## Edits kept (each REAL — cited trace — and GENERAL — class rule, no task literal)

- **E1 (code, tools.py `update_reservation_passengers`)** — in-body guard: if a passenger's
  (first,last) name == the account holder's and the dob differs, snap dob to the profile
  dob. CHECK: ran the snippet on task-17 args → `Omar Rossi 1960-12-01` → `1970-06-06`;
  no-op on task-22 args (already `1970-06-06`); other passengers untouched. Class:
  account-holder-becomes-passenger with a stale dob. Touches 17 (and robustifies 22).
- **E2 (prompt R2 split a/b)** — distinguish name-typo-of-same-person (reuse dob) from
  replacing with a DIFFERENT person incl. the account holder (use the new person's OWN
  dob). Worked examples for both. Class: any passenger-replacement. Touches 17; 22 already
  complies. CHECK: read against 17 fail trials (used 1960-12-01) vs 22 pass (1970-06-06).
- **E3 (prompt R7 + base-confirm reconcile)** — once the change is fully specified and the
  user has stated it, go straight to the write; don't spend a turn on a bare "reply yes"
  that the user's ###STOP### will cut off before execution; softness clause ties it to the
  graded outcome. Class: every single, clearly-stated DB change. Touches 40 (all trials
  stall identically), helps 12/37. CHECK: 40 t0/t1/t2 all end at "yes###STOP###" with no
  write; passing 11-t0/19/22 already execute right after an explicit go-ahead (so no
  regression — the write is unchanged, only the dead confirm turn is removed).
- **E4 (prompt R8)** — do every feasible request before transferring; transfer only the
  infeasible part. Class: multi-request tasks mixing feasible + transfer-only items.
  Touches 37 (t0 transferred wholesale, skipped the M20IZO upgrade that t1/t2 did → pass).
- **E5 (prompt R4 strengthen)** — a cabin change is ALWAYS in-place `update_reservation_flights`
  on the same id; NEVER cancel+rebook/new-booking; "basic economy flights can't be modified"
  governs FLIGHTS not CABIN. Class: all cabin changes incl. basic economy. Touches 11 (t2
  booked a new reservation → fail; t0/t1 updated in place → pass).
- **E6 (prompt R9)** — fire a user's conditional fallback only when its stated condition
  holds; otherwise solve the real obstacle toward the primary goal. Class: request+gated-fallback.
  Touches 8 (t0 dropped passenger on no-seats though fallback was price-gated; t1/t2 kept both → pass).
- **E7 (prompt R10)** — when replacing a reservation with new booking(s), cancel the original.
  Class: rebook-to-replace (e.g. multi-certificate split). Touches 23 (gold = cancel + book×3;
  all trials booked but never cancelled). Lower confidence — 23 is complex; this removes one
  clear root cause (the missing cancel) but other steps may still miss.

## Verify-the-fix
- E1 unit-logic tested (tau2 runtime not importable here — missing `loguru`; per guidance
  did not install). Guard is try/except-wrapped, cannot raise, no-op on correct input.
- Prompt edits read against the exact fail-vs-pass trial pairs cited above; each states a
  general condition, carries a worked example for the mid (gpt-oss-120b) reader, and keeps a
  softness clause so the reward-maximizing agent may deviate when literal compliance would
  cost the graded outcome.

## Preserve (must NOT regress): 19, 22, 25
- 19 (insurance cancel), 22 (same scenario as 17 but already-correct dob), 25 (split-payment
  booking). All execute their writes right after an explicit user go-ahead; R7 only removes a
  dead confirm turn, never changes a write. R2(b)/E1 are no-ops when the dob is already right
  (verified on 22). None of R4/R8/R9/R10 changes these tasks' trajectories.

## Deliberately skipped
- Task 12 (bags not added after the user said "please leave everything unchanged"): genuinely
  ambiguous — the user appears to retract, yet gold still writes the bag count. A general
  "do it anyway" rule risks firing when a user truly wants nothing changed. Not worth the
  regression risk; R7/R9 nudge toward completing un-retracted requests without hard-coding it.
- New composite `change_cabin` / additive modify tool: JOURNAL records it REFUTED in a prior
  run (model kept the corruptible primitive path); removing the primitives is unsafe because
  flight-changing tasks (23 rebook, 37 upgrade) legitimately need `update_reservation_flights`.
  So cluster 3 is fixed in prose (R4), not by a new tool.
